messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired (PD-7231) — service=auth-token-verify — severity=P1 — high error rate in token validation (spike started ~03:12 UTC). Logs show a mix of 401 signature_invalid and 'kid not found'. See https://pagerduty.example/PD-7231

pagerduty: Page sent to rotation `sre-oncall`. Escalation policy applied.

Maya (oncall): ack — I'm on it, jumping in now. Pulling logs and metrics.

Maya (oncall): quick summary: EU region first alerted, about ~5% of validation requests returning 401s for ~15m. Reproducible locally with token from auth-service: validator fails with `kid not found`.

Kevin R: I can confirm from verifier logs: repeated errors like `jwks: kid 8b3a not found` coming from verifier pods. Rotation job shows new key issued at 03:09 UTC.

Evelyn S: Support reports a handful of customers saw sign-in failures and some API calls that embed user tokens failing. Triage: customers affected ~10-15 tenants, intermittent. CS drafting comms.

Nikhil (security): Was there a scheduled key rollover? I see a cron triggered rotation at 03:09 — who executed?

Maya (oncall): rotation pipeline ran automatically (rotation-service). It looks like signing service picked up new key and started issuing tokens with kid=8b3a, but verifier fleet caches weren't invalidated/provisioned with the new JWKS entries before traffic hit. Race between signer rollout and verifier cache propagation.

Maya (oncall): immediate mitigation proposal: enable remote JWKS fetch on verifier pods on miss + accept previous key for a short TTL. I'll try a canary.

Kevin R: pushing an env toggle to canary verifiers: `ALLOW_REMOTE_JWKS_FETCH=true` and bump cache TTL to 600s.

Kevin R: (code)
```
# k8s patch
kubectl set env deploy/verifier-canary ALLOW_REMOTE_JWKS_FETCH=true
kubectl set env deploy/verifier-canary JWKS_CACHE_TTL=600
```

Maya (oncall): canary metrics look good — error rate on canary drops from 4.8% -> 0.4% within 90s. Applying to remaining verifiers now.

Support Pager: Customer comms draft: "We experienced an intermittent auth validation issue due to key rotation propagation. Services may have returned 401 for a short window (~03:12–03:29 UTC). Engineers mitigated and customers should be back to normal. Follow-up postmortem will be provided." Ready to send pending final impact numbers.

Maya (oncall): full rollout of mitigation complete at 03:29 UTC across regions. Monitoring for 10m.

incident-bot: PagerDuty incident PD-7231 acknowledged by Maya (oncall).

Kevin R: after global rollout, token validation success rates returned to baseline by ~03:33 UTC. No additional errors in the subsequent 25m. Prelim metrics: 12 tenants clearly impacted, peak error rate ~5%, median affected window ~17 minutes.

Maya (oncall): I'm going to close the page once PD is marked resolved. Postmortem items: change rotation ordering (pre-provision keys to verifiers), add explicit JWKS propagation metric, make rotation a two-phase commit, and add automated cache pre-warm.

Nikhil (security): also suggest we add a safety check to block signer from issuing tokens with new kid until at least N verifiers confirm presence.

Customer Success Bot: Support ticket CS-4321 created for affected tenants; CS to follow up with tailored comms.

Maya (oncall): handing off investigation/writeup to Kevin R for postmortem. Next oncall (Evan) arrives at 04:30 UTC — leaving notes in rotation channel.

Kevin R: taking handoff. I'll open the postmortem doc, include timelines, logs, and a remediation plan.

Maya (oncall): additional notes for writeup: rotation job timestamp 03:09:12; first 401 spike 03:12:07; mitigation canary change at 03:24:40; global mitigation applied 03:29:10. Need better observable for JWKS propagation (per-region).

incident-bot: Incident PD-7231 marked resolved by Maya (oncall). Closing page. :white_check_mark:

Maya (oncall): closing the slack thread here — follow-up postmortem will be posted to #postmortems and a changelog ticket assigned to eng-inf. Thanks all for fast response.
